---- MODULE W4Od9m0p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, VerBound, MaxLoad, Threshold

\* NoStamp marks an instance that currently holds no version snapshot (kept as an
\* out-of-range Nat so it stays comparable with real version numbers)
NoStamp == VerBound

VARIABLES version, stamp, holding, load

vars == <<version, stamp, holding, load>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..(VerBound - 1)
  /\ stamp \in [Instances -> 0..VerBound]
  /\ holding \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ load \in 0..MaxLoad

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ stamp = [i \in Instances |-> NoStamp]
  /\ holding = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ load = 0

\* Take an optimistic snapshot of the actuator's version once shedding is actually needed
StageRead(i) ==
  /\ load >= Threshold
  /\ stamp[i] = NoStamp
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![i] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, holding, load>>

\* Commit succeeds only if the version is free (even) and unchanged since the snapshot
CommitLock(i) ==
  /\ stamp[i] # NoStamp
  /\ version % 2 = 0
  /\ stamp[i] = version
  /\ version' = (version + 1) % VerBound
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![i] = NoStamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED load

\* A stale snapshot, or an actuator already held, forces the instance to retry later
RetryFail(i) ==
  /\ stamp[i] # NoStamp
  /\ (stamp[i] # version \/ version % 2 = 1)
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![i] = NoStamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, holding, load>>

\* The holder gives up the actuator, flipping the version so stale snapshots must retry
Release(i) ==
  /\ holding[i]
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ version' = (version + 1) % VerBound
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, load>>

RaiseLoad ==
  /\ load < MaxLoad
  /\ load' = load + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, stamp, holding>>

LowerLoad ==
  /\ load > 0
  /\ load' = load - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, stamp, holding>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances : StageRead(i) \/ CommitLock(i) \/ RetryFail(i) \/ Release(i)
  \/ RaiseLoad
  \/ LowerLoad

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A i \in Instances : WF_vars(CommitLock(i) \/ RetryFail(i))
  /\ \A i \in Instances : WF_vars(Release(i))

\* Mutual exclusion: the shared actuator can never be held by two instances at once
MutualExclusion ==
  \A i \in Instances : holding[i] => (\A j \in Instances \ {i} : ~holding[j])

\* Every staged snapshot is eventually resolved, either committed or retried away
StagedEventuallyResolves ==
  \A i \in Instances : (stamp[i] # NoStamp) ~> (stamp[i] = NoStamp)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    VerBound = 4
    MaxLoad = 3
    Threshold = 2
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY StagedEventuallyResolves
nl:
A regional power-grid load shedder protects a single critical shedding actuator: the
physical relay bank that actually disconnects a distribution feeder when demand gets too
high. Two independent feeder-controller instances watch the same grid segment and share
that one actuator pool, but only one of them may be driving it at any moment. Rather than
taking a hard lock up front, each instance uses optimistic locking with retry: it first
takes a lightweight snapshot of the actuator's version counter, and only afterward tries
to commit its claim to the actuator by checking that the version has not moved since the
snapshot was taken.

The version counter toggles between an even value (actuator free) and an odd value
(actuator held) every time it changes. An instance stages a snapshot of the current
version only once grid load has actually crossed the shedding threshold. If, when it
attempts to commit, the live version still matches its stale snapshot and the actuator is
free, the commit succeeds: the instance becomes the holder and the version flips to odd.
If the version has since moved -- because the other instance grabbed the actuator first,
or because the actuator is currently held -- the attempt fails and the instance must
discard its snapshot and retry later. Whoever is holding the actuator eventually releases
it, flipping the version back to even so a waiting instance's next attempt can succeed.
Independently of all this, the grid's load level itself keeps drifting up and down as
demand changes throughout the day.

The full action set is: StageRead (an instance snapshots the current version once load is
at or above the shedding threshold), CommitLock (an instance whose snapshot still matches
the live, even version becomes the actuator holder), RetryFail (an instance whose snapshot
is stale or finds the actuator held discards it), Release (the current holder gives up the
actuator and flips the version), RaiseLoad (grid load increases by one step), and
LowerLoad (grid load decreases by one step).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shedding actuator is never held by both feeder-controller instances at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every instance that stages a version snapshot eventually resolves it, either by committing the lock or by retrying it away.

---- MODULE W4Od16m6p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Pharmacists, MaxVersion, LeaseTicks

\* NoHolder marks that the lease is currently free
NoHolder == "noHolder"

VARIABLES leaseHolder, heldVersion, version, leaseAge, lastWriter

vars == <<leaseHolder, heldVersion, version, leaseAge, lastWriter>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leaseHolder \in Pharmacists \cup {NoHolder}
  /\ heldVersion \in [Pharmacists -> 0..(MaxVersion - 1)]
  /\ version \in 0..(MaxVersion - 1)
  /\ leaseAge \in 0..LeaseTicks
  /\ lastWriter \in Pharmacists \cup {NoHolder}

Init ==
  /\ leaseHolder = NoHolder
  /\ heldVersion = [p \in Pharmacists |-> 0]
  /\ version = 0
  /\ leaseAge = 0
  /\ lastWriter = NoHolder

\* A pharmacist takes the free lease and snapshots the record's current version
AcquireLease(p) ==
  /\ leaseHolder = NoHolder
  /\ leaseHolder' = p
  /\ heldVersion' = [heldVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ leaseAge' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, lastWriter>>

\* Time passes while the current holder works slowly on their edit
Tick ==
  /\ leaseHolder # NoHolder
  /\ leaseAge < LeaseTicks
  /\ leaseAge' = leaseAge + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, heldVersion, version, lastWriter>>

\* The lease's tick budget ran out; it is reclaimed without any commit happening
ExpireLease ==
  /\ leaseHolder # NoHolder
  /\ leaseAge >= LeaseTicks
  /\ leaseHolder' = NoHolder
  /\ leaseAge' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<heldVersion, version, lastWriter>>

\* Only the current holder, with a snapshot matching the live version, may commit
CommitEdit(p) ==
  /\ leaseHolder = p
  /\ heldVersion[p] = version
  /\ version' = (version + 1) % MaxVersion
  /\ lastWriter' = p
  /\ leaseHolder' = NoHolder
  /\ leaseAge' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED heldVersion

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : AcquireLease(p)
  \/ Tick
  \/ ExpireLease
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : CommitEdit(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: a live lease holder's snapshot always matches the record's live
\* version, so their eventual commit can never silently overwrite a newer edit
NoLostUpdates ==
  leaseHolder # NoHolder => heldVersion[leaseHolder] = version

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Pharmacists = {ph1, ph2}
    MaxVersion = 3
    LeaseTicks = 2
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser keeps a single shared prescription record that two
staff pharmacists can edit: the record's version number moves forward by one every time
someone successfully commits a change to it. Rather than locking the record forever,
the dispenser hands out a time-bounded lease: a pharmacist must hold the lease to edit
the record, and the lease carries a generation snapshot of the record's version taken at
the moment it was granted.

A pharmacist may be slow -- perhaps double-checking dosages or interruptions at the
counter -- but is never assumed to have crashed. While a pharmacist holds the lease, a
tick of the clock can pass representing that slow, in-progress work. If the lease's
allotted ticks run out before the pharmacist commits, the lease simply expires and
becomes available again; the slow pharmacist keeps their private, now-stale generation
snapshot around, but the dispenser must never let a stale snapshot fool it into applying
a commit for a version of the record that has already moved on -- that would silently
lose whichever update actually landed later. A commit is therefore honored only when the
committing pharmacist still actually holds the lease and their held snapshot equals the
record's current version.

The full action set is: AcquireLease (a pharmacist takes the currently free lease and
snapshots the record's version), Tick (time passes while the current lease holder works
slowly), ExpireLease (the lease's tick budget runs out and it is reclaimed without a
commit), and CommitEdit (the current lease holder, whose snapshot still matches the live
version, commits the edit and the record's version advances).
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a pharmacist currently holds the lease, their held version snapshot always equals the record's live version, so no commit can ever be built on a stale read and no update is ever lost underneath it.

---- MODULE W4Od17m5p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Quorum, MaxBags

\* NoProposer marks that no proposal is currently active
NoProposer == "noProposer"

\* The divert gate is free when nobody currently holds it
GateFree(holding) == \A m \in Nodes : ~holding[m]

VARIABLES proposer, votes, holding, bagCount

vars == <<proposer, votes, holding, bagCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ proposer \in Nodes \cup {NoProposer}
  /\ votes \subseteq Nodes
  /\ holding \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ bagCount \in 0..MaxBags

Init ==
  /\ proposer = NoProposer
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ holding = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
  /\ bagCount = 0

\* A node proposes to use the free gate, only when no proposal is already in flight
Propose(n) ==
  /\ proposer = NoProposer
  /\ GateFree(holding)
  /\ proposer' = n
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, bagCount>>

\* Any node may cast its (possibly slow-to-arrive) vote for the active proposal
CastVote(n) ==
  /\ proposer # NoProposer
  /\ n \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposer, holding, bagCount>>

\* Once a quorum of votes is in, the proposer becomes the sole gate holder
GrantAccess ==
  /\ proposer # NoProposer
  /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![proposer] = TRUE]
  /\ proposer' = NoProposer
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED bagCount

\* The holder releases the gate; one more bag has now been routed
ReleaseGate(n) ==
  /\ holding[n]
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ bagCount' = (bagCount + 1) % (MaxBags + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposer, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Propose(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : CastVote(n)
  \/ GrantAccess
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : ReleaseGate(n)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A n \in Nodes : WF_vars(CastVote(n))
  /\ WF_vars(GrantAccess)
  /\ \A n \in Nodes : WF_vars(ReleaseGate(n))

\* Mutual exclusion: the divert gate can never be held by two nodes at once
MutualExclusion ==
  \A n \in Nodes : holding[n] => (\A m \in Nodes \ {n} : ~holding[m])

\* Every active proposal is eventually granted, since a slow node's vote always arrives
ProposalsEventuallyGranted ==
  proposer # NoProposer ~> proposer = NoProposer

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxBags = 2
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY ProposalsEventuallyGranted
nl:
An airport baggage router controls a single critical resource: the divert gate that
physically switches a bag off the main belt onto a connecting-flight spur. Three router
nodes sit along the belt and any one of them may need to swing the gate, but only one may
actually be driving it at a time. Instead of a simple lock, the routers use quorum voting
on each action: before a node may take the gate, it first proposes to use it, and the
proposal is only granted once a quorum of the nodes has cast a vote in favor.

A node can be slow to cast its vote -- perhaps it is mid-way through scanning a barcode --
but it is never assumed to fail outright, so its vote is always still coming eventually.
Once a proposing node collects votes from at least a quorum of the router nodes, the
proposal is granted and that node becomes the sole holder of the divert gate. The holder
later releases the gate, which also counts one more bag as successfully routed, clearing
the way for the next proposal.

The full action set is: Propose (a node proposes to use the free divert gate when no
proposal is already active), CastVote (a node casts its vote for the currently active
proposal), GrantAccess (once at least a quorum of nodes has voted, the proposing node
becomes the gate holder), and ReleaseGate (the current holder releases the gate and the
routed-bag counter advances).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the divert gate is never held by two router nodes at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every active proposal is eventually granted, because a slow node's vote always arrives in the end.

---- MODULE W4Od12m4p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Requests, QueueCap, MaxUnits

\* The set of request ids currently sitting anywhere in the queue sequence
QueueSet(q) == {q[k] : k \in DOMAIN q}

VARIABLES queue, dispensed, unitsAvailable, overrideCount

vars == <<queue, dispensed, unitsAvailable, overrideCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Requests)
  /\ Len(queue) <= QueueCap
  /\ dispensed \subseteq Requests
  /\ unitsAvailable \in 0..MaxUnits
  /\ overrideCount \in 0..MaxUnits

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ dispensed = {}
  /\ unitsAvailable = MaxUnits
  /\ overrideCount = 0

\* Backpressure: a request is admitted only if it has room and is not already handled
Enqueue(r) ==
  /\ r \notin dispensed
  /\ r \notin QueueSet(queue)
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed, unitsAvailable, overrideCount>>

\* The front of the queue irreversibly consumes one physical unit and leaves the queue
DispenseHead ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ unitsAvailable > 0
  /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {Head(queue)}
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ unitsAvailable' = unitsAvailable - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED overrideCount

\* A queued, not-yet-dispensed request may be withdrawn without consuming a unit
CancelRequest(r) ==
  /\ r \in QueueSet(queue)
  /\ r \notin dispensed
  /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA x : x # r)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed, unitsAvailable, overrideCount>>

\* A privileged admin dispenses a specific request immediately, out of queue order
AdminOverride(r) ==
  /\ r \notin dispensed
  /\ unitsAvailable > 0
  /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {r}
  /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA x : x # r)
  /\ unitsAvailable' = unitsAvailable - 1
  /\ overrideCount' = overrideCount + 1

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Requests : Enqueue(r)
  \/ DispenseHead
  \/ \E r \in Requests : CancelRequest(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requests : AdminOverride(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A dispensed request can never resurface in the queue, so it can never be redispensed
NoDoubleDispense ==
  \A r \in Requests : r \in dispensed => r \notin QueueSet(queue)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Requests = {r1, r2, r3}
    QueueCap = 2
    MaxUnits = 2
INVARIANT NoDoubleDispense
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker manages a bounded work queue of dispense requests against
a fixed pool of physical blood units. Requests enter a queue with a hard capacity limit;
once the queue is full, the tracker applies backpressure and refuses to admit any new
request until room frees up. An ordinary worker processes the queue strictly from the
front: it pulls the head request and irreversibly dispenses one physical unit for it,
which is an action that can never be undone or repeated for that same request.

A privileged admin can override the ordinary queue order for a genuine emergency,
pulling a specific request out of line and dispensing a unit for it immediately -- but the
override still goes through the very same irreversible bookkeeping as an ordinary
dispense, so the request is marked dispensed and removed from the queue in the same step.
A request may also be withdrawn from the queue before it is ever dispensed, for example
because the patient no longer needs it; a withdrawn request simply disappears without
ever consuming a unit.

The full action set is: Enqueue (a not-yet-dispensed, not-already-queued request is
admitted if the queue has room), DispenseHead (the request at the front of the queue
irreversibly consumes one physical unit and leaves the queue), CancelRequest (a queued,
not-yet-dispensed request is withdrawn without consuming a unit), and AdminOverride (a
privileged admin dispenses a specific not-yet-dispensed request immediately, pulling it
out of the queue if it was waiting there).
SAFETY PROPERTY: once a request has been irreversibly dispensed, it can never again be found sitting in the work queue, which is exactly what keeps every dispense a one-time event.

---- MODULE W4Od9m2p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES phase, vote, crashed, executed, epoch

vars == <<phase, vote, crashed, executed, epoch>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in {"collecting", "committed", "aborted"}
  /\ vote \in [Participants -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Participants
  /\ executed \in [Participants -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch

Init ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ vote = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ executed = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ epoch = 1

\* A live participant that hasn't yet voted casts a yes or no vote for this round
Vote(p) ==
  \E b \in {"yes", "no"} :
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ vote[p] = "none"
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, crashed, executed, epoch>>

\* A participant goes silently quiet before ever voting -- it never votes again
CrashSilently(p) ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ vote[p] = "none"
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ crashed' = {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, vote, executed, epoch>>

\* Every live (non-crashed) participant voted yes: the round is committed
DecideCommit ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ Participants \ crashed # {}
  /\ \A p \in Participants \ crashed : vote[p] = "yes"
  /\ phase' = "committed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, crashed, executed, epoch>>

\* A live participant voted no: the round is aborted instead
DecideAbort ==
  /\ phase = "collecting"
  /\ \E p \in Participants \ crashed : vote[p] = "no"
  /\ phase' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, crashed, executed, epoch>>

\* Only a live yes-voter in a currently committed round may execute the shed action
Execute(p) ==
  /\ phase = "committed"
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ vote[p] = "yes"
  /\ executed' = [executed EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, vote, crashed, epoch>>

\* A decided round closes; a fresh round begins with a strictly higher epoch number
StartNextEpoch ==
  /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ phase' = "collecting"
  /\ vote' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, executed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Vote(p)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : CrashSilently(p)
  \/ DecideCommit
  \/ DecideAbort
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Execute(p)
  \/ StartNextEpoch

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A p \in Participants : WF_vars(Vote(p))
  /\ WF_vars(DecideCommit \/ DecideAbort)
  /\ WF_vars(StartNextEpoch)

\* No stale or unauthorized action: a current-epoch execution always coincides with a
\* live, currently-committed, currently-yes-voting participant, never a crashed or stale one
NoStaleExecution ==
  \A p \in Participants :
    (executed[p] = epoch) => (phase = "committed" /\ vote[p] = "yes" /\ p \notin crashed)

\* Every round still collecting votes is eventually decided one way or the other
CollectingEventuallyDecides ==
  phase = "collecting" ~> phase # "collecting"

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {pa1, pa2, pa3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT NoStaleExecution
PROPERTY CollectingEventuallyDecides
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A power-grid load shedder coordinates a synchronized shed action across three feeder
participants using two-phase commit. For each shedding round, every participant that is
still alive must first cast a yes-or-no vote on whether it is safe for it to shed load
right now; only once every live participant has voted yes does the coordinator declare
the round committed, and only then may a participant actually execute the shed action
for that round.

Exactly one participant can crash silently, and it always does so before ever casting a
vote in the round it crashes during -- it simply goes quiet instead of responding, rather
than voting no. The coordinator must not wait forever on a silently crashed participant:
the commit decision only ever depends on the votes of the participants that are still
alive. A round that gets a live no vote is aborted instead of committed. Once a round is
decided, either way, a fresh round begins: votes are cleared and a new round number
starts, bounded so it wraps back around rather than growing forever.

The full action set is: Vote (a live participant that has not yet voted in the current
round casts yes or no), CrashSilently (a participant that has not yet voted goes silently
quiet for the rest of time, before ever casting a vote), DecideCommit (every live
participant has voted yes, so the round is declared committed), DecideAbort (some live
participant voted no, so the round is declared aborted), Execute (a participant that
voted yes in a now-committed round actually carries out the shed action for that round),
and StartNextEpoch (a decided round closes and a fresh round begins).
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a participant's recorded execution matches the current round number, that participant is, at that very moment, a live yes-voter in a currently committed round -- no crashed or stale participant's action is ever recorded as authorized.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every round that is still collecting votes eventually gets decided, because a live participant's vote always eventually arrives.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Vendors, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, localVersion, authorized, crashed, lastWriter

vars == <<version, localVersion, authorized, crashed, lastWriter>>

Valid(v) == authorized[v] /\ ~crashed[v]

Init ==
  /\ version = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ localVersion = [v \in Vendors |-> 0]
  /\ authorized = [v \in Vendors |-> TRUE]
  /\ crashed = [v \in Vendors |-> FALSE]
  /\ lastWriter = [m \in Machines |-> "None"]

FetchVersion(v, m) ==
  /\ ~crashed[v]
  /\ localVersion' = [localVersion EXCEPT ![v] = version[m]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, authorized, crashed, lastWriter>>

CommitUpdate(v, m) ==
  /\ Valid(v)
  /\ localVersion[v] = version[m]
  /\ version[m] < MaxVersion
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
  /\ localVersion' = [localVersion EXCEPT ![v] = version[m] + 1]
  /\ lastWriter' = [lastWriter EXCEPT ![m] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, crashed>>

ClearStaleCustody(v) ==
  [m \in Machines |-> IF lastWriter[m] = v THEN "None" ELSE lastWriter[m]]

RevokeAuthorization(v) ==
  /\ authorized[v]
  /\ authorized' = [authorized EXCEPT ![v] = FALSE]
  /\ lastWriter' = ClearStaleCustody(v)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, localVersion, crashed>>

CrashSilently(v) ==
  /\ ~crashed[v]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![v] = TRUE]
  /\ lastWriter' = ClearStaleCustody(v)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, localVersion, authorized>>

Reauthorize(v) ==
  /\ ~authorized[v]
  /\ ~crashed[v]
  /\ authorized' = [authorized EXCEPT ![v] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, localVersion, crashed, lastWriter>>

Next ==
  \/ \E v \in Vendors, m \in Machines : FetchVersion(v, m)
  \/ \E v \in Vendors, m \in Machines : CommitUpdate(v, m)
  \/ \E v \in Vendors : RevokeAuthorization(v)
  \/ \E v \in Vendors : CrashSilently(v)
  \/ \E v \in Vendors : Reauthorize(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorizedFreshWriterOnly ==
  \A m \in Machines : lastWriter[m] # "None" => Valid(lastWriter[m])

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in [Machines -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ localVersion \in [Vendors -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ authorized \in [Vendors -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ crashed \in [Vendors -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ lastWriter \in [Machines -> Vendors \union {"None"}]

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Machines = {m1, m2}
  Vendors = {v1, v2}
  MaxVersion = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AuthorizedFreshWriterOnly
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A regional vending machine network lets field vendors remotely restock and adjust prices on machines using an optimistic-locking protocol over an unreliable wireless link. Before writing to a machine's inventory record, a vendor first fetches the record's current version counter; the vendor's handheld terminal caches this version alongside the change it intends to make. When the vendor is ready to commit, the machine only accepts the write if the vendor's cached version still equals the machine's live version counter, meaning the record was not modified by anyone else since the last fetch. If the versions disagree the commit is simply not enabled, and the vendor is expected to re-fetch and retry with a fresh version.

Each vendor additionally requires a valid dispatch credential (authorization) issued by network operations, and this credential can be revoked mid-session, for example after a vendor's route is reassigned to someone else. Because vendors carry cheap handheld terminals that periodically go offline for good with no distress signal, a vendor's terminal may crash silently at any time; nobody else in the network is notified, and the vendor simply stops taking any further actions from that point on. To keep the network's audit trail trustworthy, whenever a vendor is revoked or discovered crashed, operations proactively invalidates that vendor's most recently recorded write on every machine it touched, so the chain of custody for that machine is marked as needing re-validation until a currently-valid vendor writes to it again.

Vendors otherwise operate independently of one another: any non-crashed vendor may fetch a machine's live version at any time, may commit its pending update only if its cached version is still fresh and its credential is currently valid, may have its credential revoked by operations, may have its terminal crash silently, or may be re-authorized by operations after a review -- but only while its terminal is still alive, since a silently crashed terminal never comes back online.

A public library runs its book-reservation system across a small cluster of replica servers so that patrons can still file holds even if one machine goes down. At any time exactly one replica acts as the leader, and only the leader is allowed to accept a patron's reservation request and durably commit it into the shared reservation record; the other replicas hold their own local copies of the record that are kept in sync by asynchronous replication in the background.

If the current leader's process crashes, it crashes silently: there is no graceful shutdown message, the rest of the cluster simply notices (eventually) that the leader is unresponsive and must fail over. The failover protocol is deliberately conservative about data loss: a replica is only allowed to take over as the new leader once its own local copy of the record already contains every reservation that has ever been committed cluster-wide. This prevents the classic failover hazard where a freshly-promoted leader "forgets" a reservation that patrons were already told succeeded, silently reverting or overwriting a shared record that other patrons may already be relying on.

Because only one machine is ever leader at a time and a crash is permanent for the machine it happens to, the model keeps at least one replica alive at every moment so that a new leader can always eventually be found; reservation requests keep arriving from patrons independently of whatever is happening to the cluster's leadership.

A university library owns exactly one rare-book reading carrel that can only ever be occupied by a single patron at a time, and granting access to it is coordinated by a two-phase commit protocol across the library's branch desks. When a patron requests the carrel, a coordinator opens a transaction: every branch desk must first independently confirm, in a prepare phase, that it has no record of a conflicting hold before the carrel is actually granted. While a request is being prepared, no other patron may start a competing request for the same carrel, and once the carrel is actually granted to a patron no new request can begin until that patron releases it or is removed. A patron who is done simply releases the carrel on their own. A hospital's operating-room scheduler keeps a bounded backlog of surgery requests waiting to be assigned a room. Surgeons submit requests over an asynchronous messaging fabric that does not preserve order: a request message sent earlier can be delivered to the scheduler later than one sent afterward, and two operating-room-freed notifications can likewise arrive out of sequence. Because the fabric offers no ordering guarantee, the scheduler must never rely on messages showing up in send order, only on what has actually been delivered so far.

The scheduler enforces backpressure: an arriving request message only gets admitted into the bounded backlog if the backlog currently has room; otherwise the request message simply keeps waiting out on the fabric; undelivered messages, being unordered, may end up admitted in a completely different order than they were sent. Once a request is admitted into the backlog, the dispatcher may assign it to any currently-free operating room, which immediately removes it from the backlog (freeing a backlog slot for another waiting request) and marks that room occupied. When a room's surgery finishes, the room does not instantly become available -- it first emits a room-freed notification onto the same unordered fabric, and only once that notification is actually delivered does the room become selectable for a new assignment.

Because operating rooms are a scarcer resource than backlog slots, the scheduler's real test is whether every request that is ever sent still eventually gets an operating room, even though delivery order is completely scrambled and the number of rooms is smaller than the number of requests that may be outstanding at once.

The full action set is: SendRequest (a surgeon sends a new request message onto the unordered fabric), AdmitRequest (the scheduler delivers a pending request message into the bounded backlog, only if the backlog is not already full), DispatchToOR (the dispatcher assigns a backlogged request to a currently-free operating room, freeing a backlog slot), FinishSurgery (an occupied room's surgery completes and it emits a room-freed notification onto the fabric), and DeliverRelease (a room-freed notification is delivered, making that room selectable again).
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of requests sitting in the bounded backlog never exceeds its fixed capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every surgery request that is ever sent is eventually assigned an operating room, regardless of how the fabric reorders request and release messages.

An airport's baggage router has several diverter segments that shunt bags between conveyor lines toward the correct carousel or gate, and two independent router-controller instances -- run on separate hardware for redundancy -- both draw from the very same shared pool of segments when deciding which one gets to actively drive a given diverter. Neither controller instance talks to the other directly; the only thing keeping them from stepping on each other is the shared pool's lease bookkeeping. To actively drive a segment, a controller instance must first acquire a time-bounded lease on it from the pool; the lease carries an expiry time measured against a shared logical clock, and the instance must keep renewing the lease before it lapses if it wants to keep driving that segment.

If a controller instance goes quiet and lets its lease lapse (past its recorded expiry against the current clock), the pool reclaims the segment so it becomes available again -- crucially, reclaiming it also erases the lapsed instance's own belief that it is still in control, so that a stale controller can never keep actively driving a segment after its lease has expired and the pool has handed the segment to someone else. A controller instance may also voluntarily release a segment it holds before its lease expires. The shared logical clock advances independently of any controller's activity.

Because the two controller instances are fully independent and only coordinate through this shared pool, the entire safety of the system rests on the lease-expiry handshake being airtight: a segment must never be actively driven by both controller instances' belief state at once, whether because of a fresh acquisition, a timely renewal, a voluntary release, or a lease actually lapsing and being reclaimed.

The full action set is: Acquire (a controller instance takes an unowned segment's lease and marks itself as actively driving it), RenewLease (a controller instance extends its own still-valid lease on a segment it is currently driving), Release (a controller instance voluntarily gives up a segment it is currently driving before its lease expires), ExpireLease (the pool reclaims a segment whose lease has lapsed against the clock, and erases the lapsed instance's belief that it still drives that segment), and Tick (the shared logical clock advances by one).
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every diverter segment, at most one controller instance ever believes it is actively driving that segment at the same time.

A small warehouse operates a fleet of mobile picking robots that must periodically dock at one of a handful of physical bays to recharge or swap a battery pack. Access to each bay is protected by a time-bounded lease: a robot that wants a bay must obtain a lease token from a single shared token pool before it may occupy that bay, and the lease automatically expires after a fixed duration if the robot does not renew it. Because leases are drawn from one shared pool rather than a separate pool per bay, the fleet controller must still make sure that, bay by bay, only one robot is ever recognized as the current occupant at a time.

The mechanism works as follows. A robot with no current lease may acquire one for a bay it wants, provided the shared pool still has a free token and no other robot is currently recorded as holding that same bay; this consumes one token from the pool and stamps an expiry time computed from the current clock. While a robot still holds a bay, it may renew its lease, pushing the expiry further into the future without touching the pool. A robot may also voluntarily release its bay early, returning its token to the shared pool. Independently, a background clock advances over time, and once the clock reaches or passes a held lease's expiry time, that lease is automatically reclaimed (as if the bay controller evicted the robot), also returning the token to the shared pool. Because the pool is shared across both bay instances, a burst of acquisitions on one bay can transiently starve the other bay of tokens, but this must never cause two robots to both be treated as the current occupant of the same bay.

The full action set is: Acquire (a free robot takes an unheld bay by drawing a token from the shared pool), Renew (a robot extends the expiry of a bay it currently holds), Release (a robot voluntarily gives up a bay it holds and returns its token), Expire (the clock has passed a held lease's expiry and the bay is automatically reclaimed), and Tick (the shared background clock advances by one unit, bounded above).
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct robots are ever simultaneously recorded as holding the same bay.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every robot that currently holds a bay's lease eventually gives it up, whether by voluntary release or automatic expiry, so no robot can monopolize a bay forever.

nl:
A hospital's operating-room scheduling system assigns each surgical time slot to at most one surgical team. Instead of trusting a single dispatcher, every assignment must clear a quorum vote among a small committee of on-call schedulers before it becomes binding: this guards against any one scheduler's mistake or bias deciding who gets a room. To assign a slot, a scheduler first proposes a candidate team for that slot; other committee members then cast yes-votes for the pending proposal; only once enough committee members (a quorum) have voted yes is the assignment actually recorded as allocated.

The wrinkle is that a scheduler can crash silently at any point -- for instance their pager dies mid-shift -- and simply stops casting further votes without any notification to the rest of the committee. The committee does not roll back votes that scheduler already cast, and it does not wait for a crashed member to respond; as long as a quorum can still be reached among schedulers who do vote, the system carries on. What must never happen, regardless of who crashes or when, is that a single operating-room slot ends up recorded as allocated to two different surgical teams -- once a slot clears quorum for one team, no later proposal for that same slot may ever also clear quorum and be recorded.

The full action set is: Propose (a scheduler proposes a candidate team for a slot that has no pending proposal and is not yet allocated), CastVote (a non-crashed scheduler adds a yes-vote to a slot's pending proposal), Commit (a slot's pending proposal is recorded as allocated once its yes-votes reach quorum and the slot is not already allocated to any team), and Crash (a scheduler silently stops voting from this point on).
SAFETY PROPERTY: No operating-room slot is ever recorded as allocated to two different surgical teams.

  /\ fired \subseteq Workers
  /\ localSnapshot \in [Workers -> {"Open", "Locked", "NoSnap"}]
  /\ slowCount \in [Workers -> 0..MaxSlow]

  /\ fired = {}
  /\ localSnapshot = [w \in Workers |-> "NoSnap"]
  /\ slowCount = [w \in Workers |-> 0]

Read(w) ==

  /\ localSnapshot' = [localSnapshot EXCEPT ![w] = register]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<register, fired, slowCount>>

AttemptCommit(w) ==

  /\ register' = "Locked"
  /\ fired' = fired \cup {w}
  /\ localSnapshot' = [localSnapshot EXCEPT ![w] = "NoSnap"]
  /\ UNCHANGED slowCount

  /\ localSnapshot[w] # register
  /\ slowCount[w] < MaxSlow
  /\ localSnapshot' = [localSnapshot EXCEPT ![w] = "NoSnap"]
  /\ slowCount' = [slowCount EXCEPT ![w] = @ + 1]

  /\ register = "Open"
  /\ slowCount[w] < MaxSlow

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby is watched over by several redundant matchmaker workers, any of which may decide the lobby is full and ready to launch. Launching a match is irreversible: once the players are teleported into the game world, the lobby cannot be un-launched, so the workers must guarantee that this launch trigger fires for a given lobby exactly once, no matter how many workers are racing to be the one that flips it. The trigger itself is a single compare-and-swap register: a worker first reads a snapshot of the register, and only if the register still shows "Open" at the moment the worker acts on that snapshot does its compare-and-swap succeed in flipping it to "Locked"; if some other worker already flipped it first, the compare-and-swap simply fails and the worker must take a fresh snapshot before trying again.

None of the matchmaker workers ever crashes outright, but a worker's network hop to the register can be slow, so a worker sometimes dawdles on a snapshot it already holds, or its compare-and-swap attempt effectively times out and it must re-read before it can try again. Each worker can only be slow so many times before its connection is forced back to a fast path, so slowness is bounded rather than infinite. Despite any amount of this bounded slowness, the system must still guarantee that the lobby eventually does launch.

The full action set is: Read (a worker with no held snapshot takes a fresh snapshot of the register), AttemptCommit (a worker whose held snapshot says "Open" and whose current register is still "Open" performs a successful compare-and-swap, flipping the register to "Locked" and recording itself as the one that launched the lobby), AttemptStale (a worker whose held snapshot no longer matches the current register discards its stale snapshot), and Timeout (a worker whose held snapshot is still valid nonetheless times out before acting on it and discards the snapshot, up to a bounded number of times per worker).
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two different matchmaker workers are ever both recorded as the one that launched the same lobby.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The lobby's launch trigger is eventually flipped from "Open" to "Locked", regardless of how much bounded slowness the workers experience.

VARIABLES epoch, grantedTo, inFlight, commitLog

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in [Rooms -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ grantedTo \in [Rooms -> Coordinators \cup {NoHolder}]
  /\ inFlight \subseteq (Rooms \times Coordinators \times (0..MaxEpoch))
  /\ commitLog \subseteq (Rooms \times Coordinators \times (0..MaxEpoch))

Init ==
  /\ epoch = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]
  /\ grantedTo = [r \in Rooms |-> NoHolder]
  /\ inFlight = {}
  /\ commitLog = {}

GrantLease(room, coord) ==
  /\ grantedTo[room] = NoHolder
  /\ epoch[room] < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![room] = @ + 1]
  /\ grantedTo' = [grantedTo EXCEPT ![room] = coord]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inFlight, commitLog>>

ExpireLease(room) ==
  /\ grantedTo[room] # NoHolder
  /\ grantedTo' = [grantedTo EXCEPT ![room] = NoHolder]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inFlight, commitLog>>

SendConfirmation(room, coord) ==
  /\ grantedTo[room] = coord
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup {<<room, coord, epoch[room]>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantedTo, commitLog>>

DeliverConfirmation(room, coord, e) ==
  /\ <<room, coord, e>> \in inFlight
  /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {<<room, coord, e>>}
  /\ IF /\ epoch[room] = e
        /\ grantedTo[room] = coord
        /\ ~ \E c2 \in Coordinators, e2 \in 0..MaxEpoch : <<room, c2, e2>> \in commitLog
     THEN commitLog' = commitLog \cup {<<room, coord, e>>}
     ELSE commitLog' = commitLog
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantedTo>>

Next ==
  \/ \E room \in Rooms, coord \in Coordinators : GrantLease(room, coord)
  \/ \E room \in Rooms : ExpireLease(room)
  \/ \E room \in Rooms, coord \in Coordinators : SendConfirmation(room, coord)
  \/ \E room \in Rooms, coord \in Coordinators, e \in 0..MaxEpoch :
       DeliverConfirmation(room, coord, e)

IrreversibleAtMostOnce ==
  \A room \in Rooms :
    \A c1 \in Coordinators, e1 \in 0..MaxEpoch, c2 \in Coordinators, e2 \in 0..MaxEpoch :
      (<<room, c1, e1>> \in commitLog /\ <<room, c2, e2>> \in commitLog) => (c1 = c2 /\ e1 = e2)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

  Coordinators = {c1, c2}
  MaxEpoch = 1

nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler grants each room's current coordinating nurse a time-bounded lease before that nurse is allowed to send the one command that actually matters: the confirmation that a procedure has begun. Once a procedure-begun confirmation is accepted for a room, it is irreversible -- the room's record is permanently marked as commenced and nothing may un-commence it -- so the scheduler must guarantee that this confirmation is accepted at most once per room, no matter how the lease changes hands or how the confirmation messages travel across the hospital network.

The lease itself only controls who is currently allowed to originate a confirmation: a room with no current lease holder can have a lease granted to a nurse, tagging that grant with a fresh generation number; an existing lease can also simply expire, freeing the room to be re-leased to someone else later. Separately, the currently leased nurse may send a procedure-begun confirmation, which is stamped with the generation number that was active when it was sent and then travels across the hospital's messaging network before it is delivered. Because that network can reorder messages, a confirmation stamped with an old generation number can arrive and be delivered well after a newer lease generation has already begun for that same room -- the scheduler must recognize such a stale, out-of-order confirmation and discard it rather than let it retroactively (or redundantly) commence the room.

The full action set is: GrantLease (an unleased room's lease is granted to a nurse under a fresh generation number), ExpireLease (a room's current lease expires, freeing it), SendConfirmation (the currently leased nurse sends a procedure-begun confirmation stamped with the room's current generation number, which enters the network), and DeliverConfirmation (a confirmation is pulled off the network in any order and is accepted -- commencing the room permanently -- only if its stamped generation number still matches the room's current lease generation and that nurse is still the leaseholder and the room has not already commenced; otherwise it is silently discarded).
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every operating room, the procedure-begun confirmation is accepted and recorded at most once, and always for a single consistent nurse and generation number, regardless of any reordering of confirmation messages on the network.

  /\ assignment \in [Cranes -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ snap \in [Cranes -> Cranes \cup {NoCrane, NoSnap}]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Cranes
  /\ claimed \subseteq (Slots \times Cranes)

  /\ assignment = [cr \in Cranes |-> NoSlot]
  /\ snap = [cr \in Cranes |-> NoSnap]
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ claimed = {}

Read(cr, s) ==
  /\ cr \notin crashed
  /\ assignment[cr] = NoSlot
  /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![cr] = s]
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![cr] = occupant[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, crashed, claimed>>

AttemptCommit(cr) ==
  /\ cr \notin crashed
  /\ assignment[cr] # NoSlot
  /\ snap[cr] = NoCrane
  /\ occupant[assignment[cr]] = NoCrane
  /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![assignment[cr]] = cr]
  /\ claimed' = claimed \cup {<<assignment[cr], cr>>}
  /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![cr] = NoSlot]
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![cr] = NoSnap]

  /\ assignment[cr] # NoSlot
  /\ snap[cr] # NoSnap
  /\ ~ (snap[cr] = NoCrane /\ occupant[assignment[cr]] = NoCrane)
  /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![cr] = NoSlot]
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![cr] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, claimed, crashed>>

Crash(cr) ==
  /\ cr \notin crashed
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) < MaxCrashes
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {cr}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, assignment, snap, claimed>>

  \/ \E cr \in Cranes : AttemptCommit(cr)
  \/ \E cr \in Cranes : AttemptStale(cr)
  \/ \E cr \in Cranes : Crash(cr)

    (<<s, c1>> \in claimed /\ <<s, c2>> \in claimed) => c1 = c2

  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A cr \in Cranes, s \in Slots : SF_vars(Read(cr, s))

nl:
A container-ship crane yard has a small number of ground storage slots where incoming containers get set down. Each slot is guarded by a compare-and-swap register: a crane that wants to place a container into a particular slot first reads a snapshot of that slot's register, and only if the register is still empty at the moment the crane acts on that snapshot does its compare-and-swap succeed in claiming the slot for that crane; otherwise the compare-and-swap fails and the crane must pick a slot and take a fresh snapshot before it can try again. The yard control system must guarantee that no slot is ever double allocated -- once a slot's register has been claimed by one crane, no different crane's compare-and-swap may ever also succeed for that same slot.

Any one crane in the yard can crash silently at some point -- its motor controller locks up and it simply stops attempting further reads or swaps for good, with no alarm raised -- but the other cranes keep working. Because at most a single crane can go silent this way, and the rest keep trying slots at their own pace, the yard as a whole must still guarantee that every storage slot eventually gets claimed by some crane, even though which crane claims which slot is left to the compare-and-swap races.

The full action set is: Read (a crane with no slot currently in hand picks a slot and takes a fresh snapshot of its register), AttemptCommit (a crane whose held snapshot showed the slot empty succeeds in claiming that slot, since the register still shows empty), AttemptStale (a crane whose held snapshot showed the slot occupied, or whose snapshot has since gone stale because someone else claimed the slot first, gives up on that slot and goes back to idle), and Crash (one crane, at most, permanently and silently stops acting from this point on).
SAFETY PROPERTY: No storage slot is ever claimed by two different cranes.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every storage slot is eventually claimed by some crane, despite at most one crane crashing silently.

---- MODULE W4Od2m2p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, Authorized, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES cepoch, phase, inbox, localE, acted

vars == <<cepoch, phase, inbox, localE, acted>>

Messages == [p: Robots, e: 0..MaxEpoch, v: {"yes", "no"}]

TypeOK ==
  /\ cepoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "prepare", "committed", "aborted"}
  /\ inbox \subseteq Messages
  /\ localE \in [Robots -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ acted \subseteq Robots

Init ==
  /\ cepoch = 0
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ inbox = {}
  /\ localE = [p \in Robots |-> 0]
  /\ acted = {}

Advance ==
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "aborted"}
  /\ cepoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ cepoch' = cepoch + 1
  /\ phase' = "prepare"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, localE, acted>>

Sync(p) ==
  /\ localE[p] < cepoch
  /\ localE' = [localE EXCEPT ![p] = cepoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cepoch, phase, inbox, acted>>

SendVote(p) ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ \E v \in {"yes", "no"} :
       inbox' = inbox \cup {[p |-> p, e |-> localE[p], v |-> v]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cepoch, phase, localE, acted>>

Commit ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ \A p \in Authorized : \E m \in inbox : m.p = p /\ m.e = cepoch /\ m.v = "yes"
  /\ phase' = "committed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cepoch, inbox, localE, acted>>

Abort ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ \E p \in Authorized : \E m \in inbox : m.p = p /\ m.e = cepoch /\ m.v = "no"
  /\ phase' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cepoch, inbox, localE, acted>>

Act(p) ==
  /\ phase = "committed"
  /\ p \in Authorized
  /\ p \notin acted
  /\ \E m \in inbox : m.p = p /\ m.e = cepoch /\ m.v = "yes"
  /\ acted' = acted \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cepoch, phase, inbox, localE>>

Quiesce ==
  /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ Advance
  \/ \E p \in Robots : Sync(p)
  \/ \E p \in Robots : SendVote(p)
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ \E p \in Robots : Act(p)
  \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAction ==
  \A p \in acted :
    /\ p \in Authorized
    /\ \E m \in inbox : m.p = p /\ m.e = cepoch /\ m.v = "yes"

====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet uses a two-phase commit protocol to decide whether to carry out a shared task, such as jointly relocating a heavy pallet that requires several robots to agree before anyone moves. A coordinator opens a round by advancing to a fresh round number and entering a "prepare" phase, in which every robot that is currently on the authorized roster for this task is expected to broadcast a vote. Because the warehouse network can drop and re-deliver packets out of order, votes are modeled as messages sitting in a shared inbox rather than a strict queue: a vote is simply present or absent, and nothing guarantees it arrives in the order it was sent, so a vote tagged with an old round number can still be sitting around when a new round starts.

Each robot keeps a local belief about which round is current. Robots do not always sync this belief immediately, so a robot can cast a vote that is tagged with a round number older than the coordinator's actual round -- a "stale" vote. The coordinator only declares the round committed once every robot on the authorized roster has a "yes" vote in the inbox tagged with the exact current round number; a stale vote or a vote from a robot that is not on the authorized roster never counts toward that decision. Only after the round is committed may a robot carry out the physical action (moving the pallet), and it may only do so if its own "yes" vote for the current round is present in the inbox and it is on the authorized roster -- this is the one truly irreversible step in the scenario.

Some robots are simply never on the authorized roster for this particular task (for example, a robot from a different zone that overhears the broadcast and could still emit a vote message), and any robot's cached round belief can lag behind the coordinator's, producing exactly the stale-vote scenario the protocol must reject. The coordinator can also abort a round if any authorized robot reports "no", after which a fresh round can be opened.

The full action set is: Advance (coordinator opens a new commit round and moves to "prepare"), Sync (a robot updates its locally cached round number to match the coordinator's current round), SendVote (a robot casts a "yes" or "no" vote tagged with its own locally cached round number, right or wrong), Commit (the coordinator declares the round committed once every authorized robot has a matching "yes" vote at the current round), Abort (the coordinator abandons the round if an authorized robot voted "no"), Act (an authorized robot performs the physical pallet-move action once the round is committed and its own current-round "yes" vote is present), and Quiesce (once a round has settled into committed or aborted, the system simply holds still).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every robot that has performed the physical action is on the authorized roster and did so backed by its own "yes" vote tagged with the exact round number that was current at the time, never a stale or unauthorized one.

CONSTANTS Players, Workers, MaxVersion

VARIABLES pool, held, matched, crashed, version

vars == <<pool, held, matched, crashed, version>>

Reserved == UNION {held[w] : w \in Workers}

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \subseteq Players
  /\ held \in [Workers -> SUBSET Players]
  /\ matched \subseteq Players
  /\ crashed \subseteq Workers
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion

Init ==
  /\ pool = Players
  /\ held = [w \in Workers |-> {}]
  /\ matched = {}
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ version = 0

Reserve(w) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ held[w] = {}
  /\ \E s \in SUBSET pool :
       /\ Cardinality(s) = 2
       /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![w] = s]
       /\ pool' = pool \ s
  /\ UNCHANGED <<matched, crashed, version>>

Commit(w) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ held[w] # {}
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ matched' = matched \cup held[w]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![w] = {}]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, crashed>>

Abort(w) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ held[w] # {}
  /\ pool' = pool \cup held[w]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![w] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<matched, crashed, version>>

Crash(w) ==
  /\ w \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {w}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, matched, version>>

Reclaim(w) ==
  /\ w \in crashed
  /\ held[w] # {}
  /\ pool' = pool \cup held[w]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![w] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<matched, crashed, version>>

Idle == UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Reserve(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Commit(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Abort(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Crash(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Reclaim(w)
  \/ Idle

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A w \in Workers : WF_vars(Commit(w))
  /\ \A w \in Workers : WF_vars(Abort(w))
  /\ \A w \in Workers : WF_vars(Reclaim(w))

Conservation ==
  /\ Players = pool \cup Reserved \cup matched
  /\ pool \cap Reserved = {}
  /\ pool \cap matched = {}
  /\ Reserved \cap matched = {}

HoldsEventuallyRelease ==
  \A p \in Players : (p \in Reserved) ~> (p \notin Reserved)

====

CONSTANTS
  Players = {p1, p2, p3, p4}
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  MaxVersion = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
PROPERTY HoldsEventuallyRelease
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker holds a fixed pool of players waiting to be paired into matches. Several matchmaker workers independently try to build a match by optimistically grabbing a pair of players out of the shared lobby pool, without taking any lock first. Each worker's grab is exclusive while it holds the pair: it either commits the pair into a finished match, or it gives up and releases the pair back to the lobby pool so another worker (or itself, later) can retry with a fresh optimistic attempt. A shared version counter is bumped every time a commit succeeds, standing in for the optimistic-concurrency token that a real compare-and-swap would check before allowing a commit to land.

Every player who exists at the start of the run must always be accounted for exactly once: sitting in the lobby pool waiting, held by exactly one worker's in-flight optimistic attempt, or locked into a finished match. Players are never duplicated across these three places and never simply vanish -- the matchmaker only ever moves them between pool, in-flight hold, and finished match.

The twist is that a worker can crash silently at any point while it is holding a pair: it stops taking any further steps of its own accord (it can never again commit or voluntarily release), but the two players it was holding are not lost -- they remain reserved under that worker's name until a separate, still-live reclaim process notices the crash and returns them to the lobby pool so matchmaking can continue. Only a crashed worker's held pair can be reclaimed this way; a live worker's held pair can only be released by that worker itself, by committing or voluntarily aborting.

The full action set is: Reserve (a live, currently idle worker optimistically grabs some pair of players out of the lobby pool), Commit (a live worker with a held pair locks that pair into a finished match and bumps the shared version counter), Abort (a live worker voluntarily gives up its held pair and returns it to the lobby pool to retry later), Crash (a live worker silently and permanently stops acting on its own), Reclaim (a separate live process notices a crashed worker's held pair and returns it to the lobby pool), and Idle (once every player is either matched or stuck with no live worker left to act, the system simply holds still).
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every point in time the lobby pool, the set of in-flight held players, and the set of players locked into finished matches form a partition of the whole player set -- every player is accounted for in exactly one of the three places, with none created or destroyed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every player who is ever picked up into a worker's in-flight hold eventually leaves that hold -- either locked into a finished match or, if the holding worker crashed, returned to the lobby pool by the reclaim process.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Banks, Capacity, MaxWorkers, MaxBacklog, MaxSettled

VARIABLES queue, inProgress, settledCount, backlog

vars == <<queue, inProgress, settledCount, backlog>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Banks)
  /\ inProgress \in 0..MaxWorkers
  /\ settledCount \in 0..MaxSettled
  /\ backlog \in [Banks -> 0..MaxBacklog]

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ inProgress = 0
  /\ settledCount = 0
  /\ backlog = [b \in Banks |-> 0]

Generate(b) ==
  /\ backlog[b] < MaxBacklog
  /\ backlog' = [backlog EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inProgress, settledCount>>

Submit(b) ==
  /\ backlog[b] > 0
  /\ Len(queue) + inProgress < Capacity
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
  /\ backlog' = [backlog EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inProgress, settledCount>>

Dequeue ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ inProgress < MaxWorkers
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ inProgress' = inProgress + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<settledCount, backlog>>

Finalize ==
  /\ inProgress > 0
  /\ settledCount < MaxSettled
  /\ inProgress' = inProgress - 1
  /\ settledCount' = settledCount + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, backlog>>

Idle == UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Generate(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Submit(b)
  \/ Dequeue

  MaxWorkers = 2

INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch system accepts settlement instructions from a small set of member banks and processes them through a single shared work queue with backpressure. Each member bank accumulates its own backlog of settlement instructions that still need to be submitted into the shared batch queue. A bank may submit one backlogged instruction into the queue only if there is spare shared capacity: the queue's current length plus the number of instructions currently being processed by settlement workers must stay strictly below the fixed system capacity, otherwise the submission is simply not possible yet and the bank must wait -- this is the backpressure.

A settlement worker pulls the oldest instruction off the front of the queue into active processing, and later finishes processing it, at which point it is durably settled and no longer occupies any shared capacity at all. The system's whole point is to guarantee that the combined footprint of work sitting in the shared queue and work currently being processed never exceeds the fixed capacity of the settlement system, no matter how bursty the banks' submissions are.

One participant bank in this batch can be arbitrarily slow -- it may sit on a large backlog for a long time before submitting anything, or interleave its submissions sparsely compared to the others -- but it is never treated as failed or removed from the system, and its backlog can still grow at any time as new settlement instructions arrive for it. There is no notion of timing out or excluding a slow bank; the shared queue simply keeps enforcing backpressure against everyone equally regardless of how fast or slow any single bank happens to submit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the combined footprint of instructions sitting in the shared queue and instructions currently being processed never exceeds the settlement system's fixed capacity.

A vending machine network runs two independent local clusters, each arranged as its own token ring: within a cluster, a single circulating token passes from machine to machine in a fixed order, and only whichever machine currently holds its cluster's token may attempt to draw from the network's shared restock pool. Each item in the shared pool represents a one-time reward voucher (for example, a promotional free-item code) that must be dispensed by exactly one machine, exactly once, no matter which of the two clusters ends up being the one to dispense it.

The two clusters never merge their tokens and never coordinate directly with each other -- each ring just keeps rotating its own token independently, on its own schedule -- but both clusters read from and write into the very same shared pool record of which vouchers have already been dispensed and by whom. This shared pool is what has to keep the "exactly once" guarantee intact even though two completely independent token rotations are both allowed to reach into it.

When a machine holds its ring's token, it may attempt to dispense any voucher from the pool that has not yet been claimed by anyone in either cluster; once dispensed, that claim is permanent and irreversible -- the machine records itself as the one that handed it out, and no other machine, in either cluster, may ever dispense that same voucher afterward. nl:
A vending machine network uses quorum voting before any machine is allowed to carry out an irreversible action, such as dispensing the very last unit of a scarce promotional item. Instead of a single coordinator deciding, each machine in the network independently casts a vote endorsing a specific proposed action, and that proposal may only be carried out once a quorum -- a fixed minimum number of endorsing votes -- has been gathered for it. Votes are sent as independent messages into the network and the network itself may reorder them arbitrarily: a vote that was cast first can be delivered after one cast later, and delivery order has nothing to do with sending order.

Because delivery can be reordered, the tally that decides whether a quorum has been reached is always computed over votes that have actually been delivered, never over votes that have merely been sent but are still stranded somewhere in transit. A machine may also withdraw its endorsement for a proposal before the action has been carried out, removing its vote from both the sent and delivered records, which models a machine changing its mind before the irreversible step happens; once the action for a proposal has actually been carried out, no further withdrawal for that proposal is meaningful.

Once a proposal's delivered votes reach the required quorum size, the network carries out that proposal's action exactly once, and it permanently records the exact set of delivered votes that justified the decision. No proposal can ever be carried out a second time, and whenever a proposal has been carried out, the votes credited as its justification must all actually have been delivered and must number at least the quorum size -- a reordered-but-undelivered vote can never by itself be the basis for the action.

The full action set is: SendVote (a machine casts a vote endorsing a proposal, entering the network), Deliver (the network delivers a previously sent vote to the tally process, in no particular order relative to other sends), Execute (the network carries out a proposal's irreversible action once its delivered votes reach the quorum size, recording exactly which delivered votes justified it), Withdraw (a machine retracts its vote for a proposal that has not yet been carried out, removing it from both the sent and delivered records), and Idle (once every send, deliver, execute, and withdraw option is exhausted, the network simply holds still).
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a proposal has been carried out, the exact set of votes recorded as its justification were all actually delivered and numbered at least the quorum size, so the irreversible action for that proposal happens at most once and only on genuinely delivered endorsements.

CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2, w3}

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MutualExclusion

PROPERTY CrashReclaimed
nl:
A busy print shop runs a single high-capacity printer whose paper tray is the scarce critical resource. Before any worker's job can touch the tray, the worker must first acquire a coarse-grained lock on the whole printer cabinet, and only after holding that outer lock may it acquire a fine-grained lock on the paper tray itself. This hierarchical locking discipline exists so that a worker never fiddles with the tray while some other worker is mid-operation on the cabinet: the outer lock is grabbed first, then the inner one, and both must be released together when the job finishes.

The twist is that a worker's control software can crash silently while it is holding either the cabinet lock or the tray lock (or both) - it simply stops responding, with no warning message and no orderly release. Nothing else about the shop notices immediately. A shop floor monitor periodically scans for such stalled workers and marks them as detected; only once a crashed worker has been detected can its held locks be forcibly reclaimed and handed back to the pool, letting some other worker's job proceed. Because the monitor keeps scanning and reclaiming rather than giving up, every crash is eventually cleaned up.

Ordinary jobs cycle through requesting the cabinet lock, then the tray lock, then finishing and releasing both locks together, over and over, competing with other workers for the same two nested locks. The crash-and-reclaim path runs concurrently with this ordinary cycle, so at any moment some workers may be idle, mid-job, or stuck crashed while the monitor works through its backlog.

The full action set is: AcquireCoarse (a worker takes the free cabinet lock), AcquireFine (a worker already holding the cabinet lock takes the free tray lock), Release (a worker holding both locks finishes its job and releases both), Crash (a worker holding one or both locks silently dies), DetectCrash (the monitor notices a crashed worker), and Reclaim (the monitor forcibly frees the locks of a detected crashed worker and returns it to idle).
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a worker holds the fine-grained tray lock, that same worker must also hold the coarse-grained cabinet lock, so the critical tray resource is never accessed outside the protecting outer lock.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every worker that silently crashes while holding a lock is eventually detected and has its locks reclaimed, returning it to idle.

A university course-registration system keeps one shared record for a popular course: the number of students currently enrolled. Registering a student is carried out as a two-phase-commit transaction across two backend participants, the Registrar office and the Billing office, both of which must agree before the enrollment count is updated. When a registration transaction starts it first takes a snapshot of the record's current version number, then asks both participants to vote yes; only once both have voted, and the record's version has not moved since the snapshot was taken, may the transaction commit its increment to the enrollment count and bump the version. This version check exists precisely to stop lost updates: if some other transaction had already committed against the same version, a transaction that blindly wrote its own increment on top of a stale read would silently erase that other transaction's update.

The complication is that the Billing office's terminal can crash silently in the middle of a transaction - it just stops sending votes, with no explicit failure signal. When that happens the in-flight transaction can no longer reach unanimity and must be aborted rather than left hanging forever, releasing the transaction slot for a future attempt with a fresh snapshot.

A print shop keeps a fixed total number of blank sheets circulating through three pools: a central supply stack, the printer's loaded tray, and the finished-printed output stack. A sheet only ever moves between these three pools - loading takes a sheet from supply into the tray, and printing takes a sheet from the tray into the finished stack - so the sum of sheets across all three pools never changes, no sheet is ever created or destroyed.

Every shop attendant must weigh in before either kind of move takes effect: moving a sheet is proposed, then each attendant casts a yes vote, and only once a strict majority of attendants have voted yes does the shop actually commit the move and clear the ballot for the next proposal. Attendants are never assumed to fail outright in this shop - the twist is that an attendant can simply be slow to get to the voting station, taking an arbitrary amount of time, but it always eventually shows up and casts its vote rather than vanishing for good.

At any moment the shop may have a load-proposal, a print-proposal, or a restock-proposal pending, or no proposal at all, with some subset of attendants having already voted yes on whatever is pending. A restock move sends a sheet from the finished stack back to the supply stack, which is what keeps the shop's cycle running indefinitely instead of grinding to a halt once every sheet has been printed. Because slow attendants keep arriving rather than staying away forever, any proposal that is put up eventually gathers its majority and gets committed, clearing the way for the next one.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every proposal that is put up for a vote is eventually committed, because slow attendants always eventually arrive and vote rather than failing permanently.

    /\ crashed # {}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "aborted"]

    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED << phase, votes, openPrice, clearedRound >>

    \/ \E r \in Rounds : Clear(r)
    \/ \E r \in Rounds : AbortRound(r)

nl:
A stock exchange runs a single opening auction each morning to set the day's opening price. Because a stalled attempt must be retryable, the exchange tracks the auction as a small set of independent rounds: each round separately collects yes votes from the member trading firms in a two-phase-commit style handshake, and only a round whose votes are unanimous may proceed to actually cross the book and publish the opening price. Publishing the opening price is irreversible - once it happens the market has opened and trading history cannot be rewritten - so the exchange must guarantee that at most one round is ever allowed to perform that irreversible clearing action, no matter how many rounds were started or retried.

The complication is that a member firm's order-entry gateway can crash silently partway through a round's voting - it simply stops sending votes, with no disconnect notice. When that happens, the round it was participating in can never gather unanimous votes, so the exchange abandons that round and may start a fresh round to try again from a clean slate. Because two or more rounds might be live at once (an old stalled round alongside a fresh retry), the exchange keeps a single ledger slot recording which round, if any, has actually executed the irreversible clear, and every round's clearing action must check that ledger slot is still empty before it is allowed to write to it.

At any time some rounds may be quietly collecting votes, some may have reached full unanimity and be ready to clear, one (at most) may have actually cleared and published a price, and any round can be abandoned if a firm it depended on has crashed. The full action set is: Vote (a firm that has not crashed casts its yes vote in a round that is still collecting votes), Prepare (a round whose votes are unanimous moves to ready-to-clear), Clear (a ready round checks the single-clear ledger is still empty, then writes itself into it and publishes its opening price, an irreversible action), AbortRound (a round still collecting votes is abandoned because some firm it needed has crashed), and CrashFirm (a member firm's gateway silently stops voting).
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a round has reached the cleared phase, the single-clear ledger must record that exact round, so no two distinct rounds can ever both perform the irreversible opening-price clear.

    /\ phase = [fl \in Flights |-> "idle"]

    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![fl] = "requesting"]
    /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![fl] = s]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![fl] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED allocation

VoteYes(fl, t) ==

    /\ t \notin votes[fl]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![fl] = @ \cup {t}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << phase, request, allocation >>

GrantSlot(fl) ==

    /\ votes[fl] = Stations
    /\ allocation[request[fl]] = "free"

    /\ UNCHANGED << request, votes >>

    /\ phase[fl] = "granted"
    /\ allocation' = [allocation EXCEPT ![request[fl]] = "free"]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![fl] = "idle"]
    /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![fl] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

    /\ allocation[request[fl]] = "free"

    /\ UNCHANGED << request, votes >>

AdminForceRelease(fl) ==
    /\ phase[fl] = "granted"
    /\ allocation' = [allocation EXCEPT ![request[fl]] = "free"]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![fl] = "idle"]
    /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![fl] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED votes

nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands out fixed time slots on a single runway to waiting flights. Under normal operation, a flight requesting a slot opens a two-phase-commit round across the tower's coordinating stations: the flight names the slot it wants, each station casts a yes vote, and only once every station has voted yes, and the slot is still free, is the flight actually granted that slot. A granted flight later releases its slot, freeing it for a future request.

The twist is that a privileged admin override exists alongside the normal voting path. The admin can force-grant a flight's requested slot without waiting for the stations' votes at all, and can force-release a flight that is holding a slot - but in both cases the admin still has to respect the same free-slot check as the ordinary path, so the override can unstick a stalled negotiation without ever letting two flights hold the same slot at once. This matters because ordinary station voting is not assumed to always complete: some station can simply take arbitrarily long, or never get around to voting, and the admin override is what keeps the system from stalling forever in that case.

At any time some flights are idle, some are mid-request waiting on station votes, and some are holding a granted slot; the allocator tracks which slot (if any) each requesting flight has its eye on, and which flight (if any) currently holds each slot. The full action set is: Request (an idle flight opens a request for a specific free-looking slot), VoteYes (a station casts its yes vote for a flight's pending request), GrantSlot (a request with unanimous station votes is granted, provided the slot is still free), Release (a flight holding a granted slot gives it up), AdminForceGrant (the admin grants a pending request immediately, bypassing station votes, provided the slot is still free), and AdminForceRelease (the admin forcibly frees a flight's granted slot).
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct flights are ever simultaneously marked as granted for the same requested slot, so the same runway slot is never double-allocated.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every flight whose slot request is pending is eventually granted that slot, a guarantee that holds even if ordinary station voting stalls forever, because the admin override always eventually steps in.
